name: Philosophy - BA - Law, Ethics, and Society
narrative: A major in philosophy requires a total of fifteen philosophy courses, at least twelve of which must be upper-division (courses numbered 100 and above).

Up to two upper-division courses outside of philosophy can count among the twelve required for the major if they are drawn from a related field and contribute to the major's philosophical program; such credit must be approved by the undergraduate adviser.
Honors and directed study courses (PHIL 191–199) may not be used to satisfy the major requirement of fifteen philosophy courses.

Seven of the twelve upper-division courses in the major must be taken in the Department of Philosophy at UC San Diego. Courses taken at other institutions may be applied toward the major by petition only.
All courses applied toward the major must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a grade of C– or better. A GPA of 2.0 must be maintained in courses applied toward the major.

items.label: History of Philosophy
items.notes: These courses must be taken in order.

items.label: Two more philosophy courses
items.notes: Fifteen philosophy courses in all, at least twelve upper-division. The eight core courses and the five Law, Ethics, and Society courses count toward the fifteen (and already give at least twelve upper-division), so two more lower- or upper-division philosophy courses complete it. PHIL 191–199 may not be used. Up to two upper-division courses outside philosophy may count among the twelve with adviser approval. The catalog lets a course count for both the emphasis and a core requirement; the planner counts each course once, so it asks for five emphasis courses besides the core ones (the total is still fifteen).

sections.name: Area of Emphasis: Law, Ethics, and Society

requirement.label: Law, Ethics, and Society
requirement.notes: Students selecting an optional area of emphasis must take and pass five of the courses listed under that area. Courses taken to complete an area of emphasis are counted toward the fifteen courses required for the major and may also fulfill a core requirement. Areas of emphasis are not noted on transcripts or diplomas.
